headword: {川端康成|かわばたやすなり}
gloss: Kawabata Yasunari (1899-1972), first Japanese Nobel laureate in literature

definitions.explanation: A novelist known for spare, lyrical prose and works such as {雪国|ゆきぐに} (Snow Country) and {伊豆|いず}の{踊子|おどりこ} (The Izu Dancer). In 1968 he became the first Japanese writer to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.

{川端康成|かわばたやすなり}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧1968⟦{年|ねん}→年：09876_nen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ノー⟦ベル→ベル：01379_beru⟧⟦{文学賞|ぶんがくしょう}→文学賞：22097_bungakushou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受賞|じゅしょう}→受賞：11867_jushou⟧した。
examples.english: Kawabata Yasunari won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1968.

examples.english: The opening line of "Snow Country" — "The train came out of the long tunnel into the snow country" — is famous.

notes:
Usually called {川端|かわばた} (the family name) in casual reference.

CULTURAL NOTE:
He was the first Japanese writer to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, praised by the committee for prose that expressed "the essence of the Japanese mind." ⟦{雪国|ゆきぐに}→雪国：14608_yukiguni⟧ (Snow Country) and {伊豆|いず}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{踊子|おどりこ} (The Izu Dancer) are standard reading in Japanese literature classes; he died by suicide in 1972, about a year and a half after his colleague and protégé {三島由紀夫|みしまゆきお}.
